sources.title: Adrian Baddeley, Spatial Point Processes and their Applications
sources.locator: Complete 75-page lecture notes read; this page uses Lecture 4, PDF pp. 61–73, including §§4.3–4.6 and §4.9.

contents.name: §4.3 finite point configurations and Example 4.5 finite Poisson process, (37)
contents.support: The finite Poisson law is expanded over tuple locations and count with the 1/n! factor; the local proof compares that expansion under λθ dx and unit-rate dx.

contents.name: §4.4 Definition 4.1 and Example 4.6 unit-rate Poisson density, (42)
contents.support: A density relative to a fixed Poisson reference and the uniform Poisson density are treated directly; the local result verifies the inhomogeneous formula by integration on every measurable event.

contents.name: §4.5 equation (45), Theorem 4.1, and Example 4.8 conditional-intensity density ratio
contents.support: The source identifies conditional intensity as f(η+δu)/f(η) under the hereditary-support condition; the local lemma supplies a complete finite Mecke proof for strictly positive Gibbs densities.

contents.name: §4.6 Definition 4.2 and Example 4.11 finite Gibbs and Strauss models
contents.support: The Strauss weight β^N γ^S and conditional intensity βγ^t are used with an explicit finite normalizer and empty-boundary convention.

contents.name: §4.7 Example 4.12 homogeneous Poisson maximum likelihood
contents.support: The positive-count estimate N(W)/|W| is reproduced; the local proof adds the zero-count boundary and attainment distinction.

contents.name: §4.9 Definition 4.3 and Example 4.15 pseudolikelihood for Poisson and Strauss models
contents.support: The event-intensity product and integrated-intensity exponential define the criterion; the local Strauss example compares its data ratios with the exact Gibbs density.

sources.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process
sources.locator: Author-hosted 2017 book version; complete relevant arguments read in Chapter 3, PDF pp. 33–34, and Chapter 4, PDF pp. 39–43.

contents.name: Chapter 3 Proposition 3.5, Theorem 3.6, and Proposition 3.8 finite mixed-binomial construction and law
contents.support: The finite-intensity point-process law has Poisson total count and iid locations with normalized intensity; this is the supplier interface used in the likelihood comparison.

contents.name: Chapter 4 Theorem 4.1 and finite-intensity derivation of the Mecke equation
contents.support: The Mecke equation supplies the add-one integral identity; the local proof applies the finite-intensity form to a positive Gibbs density and derives its Papangelou ratio.

contents.name: Chapter 4 mixed-binomial finite-case proof, Theorems 4.4–4.5, multiplicity convention
contents.support: The finite law preserves atom occurrences and has product sampling locations; the local proof checks that atomless intensity makes all pairwise collision diagonals null.
